title: Peptide Vial Labels and Condensation: Apply to Dry Glass, Not a Cold Fog
seoTitle: Peptide Vial Label Condensation Guide | RP Labels
description: Plan the labeling sequence for chilled peptide vials: dew point, dry glass, application pressure and an applied-sample check before ordering custom rolls.
alt: AI-generated RP Research printed vial held beside a visibly wet unlabelled glass vial on a packaging bench
caption: AI-generated application comparison, not a documented RP production test. Printed names, code and lot are illustrative and are not validated product data.
intro: A label specified for cold storage may still fail if it is first applied to a glass vial covered in condensation.
sources: 3M: processing guidance for industrial adhesive tapes, including glass and dew point
Avery Dennison: application surface and moisture in adhesive selection

title: Supplement Facts Panel Space: Set the Dieline Before Styling the Bottle
seoTitle: Supplement Facts Panel and Label Dieline | RP Labels
description: Reserve usable width for the Supplement Facts panel, ingredients and distributor details before committing a custom supplement bottle-label dieline.
alt: AI-generated RP Wellness supplement bottle beside a flat botanical label proof with a placeholder Supplement Facts panel and red cut lines
caption: AI-generated artwork-planning concept. The panel contains placeholder lines, not approved nutrition data or regulatory-compliant finished artwork.
intro: The expensive part of a beautiful wrap label is discovering, after approval, that the information panel has nowhere to go.
sources: FDA: dietary supplement general labeling and information-panel placement
FDA: Supplement Facts panel formatting and small-package exceptions

title: HDPE Supplement Bottle Labels: Check the Plastic Before Choosing Adhesive
seoTitle: HDPE Supplement Bottle Label Adhesion | RP Labels
description: Compare label adhesion on the actual HDPE supplement bottle, including texture, panel shape, storage and edge lift, before approving a custom label stock.
alt: AI-generated RP Wellness labels on two white HDPE supplement bottles, one showing a lifting edge beside a printed roll
caption: AI-generated material-selection scenario, not a test result for any RP adhesive, bottle or production batch. Bottle copy is fictional.
intro: A white supplement bottle and a clear PET bottle can share artwork, but not necessarily the same adhesive specification.
sources: Avery Dennison: HDPE, surface energy and label adhesives

title: Hologram Seals on Corrugated Cartons: Test the Tear, Not Just the Shine
seoTitle: Hologram Seal on Corrugated Carton | RP Labels
description: Specify and sample a custom hologram seal across a corrugated carton opening: fiber tear, coating, seam geometry and evidence after removal.
alt: AI-generated holographic RP Secure carton seal across an intact flap beside an opened carton with visible fiber tear
caption: AI-generated carton-seal concept, not evidence that a particular RP construction achieves fiber tear or tamper resistance. Physical testing is required.
intro: On corrugated board, a glossy hologram is the easy part. The hard question is what the seal and carton do when someone lifts the flap.
sources: Avery Dennison: security labeling solutions including fiber tear
Avery Dennison: tamper-evident labels across carton seams

title: Duplicate QR Scans on Security Labels: Write the Response Before Printing
seoTitle: Duplicate QR Security Label Scans | RP Labels
description: Plan the customer-facing and operator response to repeated scans of a serialized QR security label without treating every repeat as counterfeiting.
alt: AI-generated RP Secure holographic QR sample labels with serials on a roll and sealed cartons beside a handheld reader
caption: AI-generated security-label concept. QR-like patterns and DEMO serials are illustrative, not functional identifiers or proof of authentication or a live verification service.
intro: A unique printed code is not a complete verification plan. You still need to decide what a second scan means and what the visitor sees.
sources: GS1: digital signatures, copied barcodes and conflicting observations
GS1: retail 2D barcode implementation and web-security considerations
